summary: This paper addresses logical qubit mapping for the Gross code, a spatially efficient quantum error correction code, by developing a two-stage compilation pipeline that reduces inter-module measurement errors. The approach uses hypergraph partitioning to cluster logical qubits and a priority-based algorithm for module assignment, achieving ~13% average reduction in non-fixed error rates and up to ~36% in optimal cases compared to existing NISQ and FTQC mappers.
motivation: Early fault-tolerant quantum architectures using high-rate qLDPC codes like the Gross code require compilation strategies that minimize program failure rates. Existing NISQ and FTQC qubit mappers are inadequate because they cannot handle the two-level clustering/assignment structure of logical qubit mapping, model only length-2 interactions instead of length-$n$ Pauli products, and neglect factory placement.
method: A two-stage pipeline first uses hypergraph partitioning (KaHyPar with $\varepsilon=0.06$) to group logical qubits into clusters that minimize modules involved per rotation, then applies a priority-based heuristic (Algorithm 1) that assigns modules based on rotation frequency to minimize inter-module measurement paths. The approach is evaluated on QASMBench circuits compiled to Pauli-Based Computation and Bicycle instructions.
result: Across benchmarks, the mapper reduces non-fixed error contribution from inter-module measurements by ~13% on average and ~22% with localized factory availability, decreases total program failure rate by ~4% on average, and reduces inter-module measurement count by up to ~62% in best cases. Compilation time is 2.61 s mean across benchmarks with no timeouts.
